Subrata Chowdhury with MA Zahed, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.

parties:
Matiur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Election Commission and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman J: In this Writ Petition on 6.3.90 under Article 102 of the Constitution this Court directed the Election Commission to consider the petition of petitioner Md. Matiur Rahman under section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. LXI of 1982) for wrong printing of the fictitious name of "Azimuddin" in place of his name at serial No. 148 of the male Electoral Roll of village Darikandi, Union Parishad Narayanpur, Upazila Belabo, District Narshingdi and to correct the mistake, if any according to the draft voter's list for the said area. 

 2. Section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. LXI of 1982) provides as follows : 

 "15. The Commission may, at any time, order the inclusion in the electoral Roll of the name of any person qualified to be enrolled on such electoral Roll and such name shall from the date of such order form part of the electoral roll" 

 3. The Chief Election Commissioner in response to this Court's direction communicated to this Court on 10.3.90 that the name "Azimuddin" was printed by mistake at serial No. 148 of the Male Electoral Roll for the said area (village Darikandi) as some one tampered with the name of petitioner Md. Matiur Rahman in the draft voters' list subsequently and the Chief Election Commissioner also informed this Court that he has directed the registering authority to insert and include the name of the petitioner (at serial No. 148) in the male Electoral Roll of the said area, that is, village Darikandi, Union Parishad Narayanpur, Upazila Belabo, District Narsingdi. In view of the repeal of Rule 68 of the Upazila Parishad (Election of Chairman) Rules, 1983 the Chief Election Commissioner took the view that there is no specific provision in law empowering him to direct Respondent No. 2 the designated Appellate Authority (The Deputy Commissioner, Narsingdi) and respondent No. 3 the Returning Officer [The Additional Deputy Commissioner (General), Narsingdi] to accept the nomination paper of the petitioner. The Chief Election Commissioner did not accept the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the Election Commissioner under their plenary powers of holding and conducting the elections fairly and properly under section 19 of The Local Government (Upazila Parishad and Upazila Administration Re-organisation) Ordinance, 1982 can set right the illegalities committed by the Returning Officer. In the case of AFM Shah Alam Vs. Mujibul Huq and others, 1989 BLD (AD) 78=41 DLR (AD) 68 it has merely been observed in paragraph 46 in a general way as follows : 

 4. The learned Advocate for the petitioner probably did not know the existence of the provision of section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 which empowers the Election Commission to order at any time the inclusion in the electoral rolls to the names of any person qualified to be enrolled on such electoral roll and, therefore failed to draw attention of the Chief Election Commissioner to the said provision in section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982. As a matter of fact even before this Court the learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to refer to the said provision and we had to tell him that along with provision of the Local Government (Upazila Parishad and Upazila Administration and Re-organisation) Ordinance, 1982 the provision of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 have also to be read. Thereafter the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that the Chief Election Commissioner failed to exercise his power under section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 which alone would have enabled the petitioner to contest in the election for the office of Chairman of Belabo Upazila Parishad. 

 7. Mr. Subrata Chowdhury, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that in accordance with the direction of this Court the Chief Election Commissioner caused an enquiry to be made into the allegation of the petitioner and finding truth in the complaint of the petitioner got the petitioner's name included in the concerned Electoral Roll in exercise of his power under section 15 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 and that in accordance with the ad interim order of this Court Respondent No. 2 (the designated Appellate Authority) and Respondent No. 3 the Returning Officer allowed the petitioner to contest the election for the office of Chairman of pazila Belabo, District Narsingdi.
